correctness.rationale: A base-Q diagonal action gives distinct weights to all degree-d monomials. For d>=3, a monomial with at least three variables has first-catalecticant rank at least three; a two-variable monomial with both exponents at least two has second-catalecticant rank at least three. The remaining fixed monomials are pure powers and tangent monomials, all of which lie in sigma_2. For d=2 every quadratic monomial has symmetric border rank at most two. Euler localization then converts these exact fixed-point counts to topological Euler characteristics, and constructible additivity gives the exact border-rank-two stratum. The bundled checker independently replays the monomial catalecticant classification over a broad finite grid.

originality.rationale: The highly relevant archival Veronese-secant literature was inspected at full-text level. Ballico--Bernardi analyze low border-rank strata and Raicu proves flattening-minor equations for the same second secant, but neither source contains an Euler-characteristic statement. Targeted semantic and web searches using geometric, symmetric-tensor, fixed-point, and characteristic-class terminology did not locate the degree-two versus degree-at-least-three Euler classification. The quadratic case is acknowledged as prior symmetric-determinantal coverage; originality rests on the higher-degree formula and the sharp phase transition, which are not implied by that boundary case. Nogueira subsequently computed topological Euler characteristics of secants to rational normal curves, which covers the n=1 specialization; this does not imply the higher-dimensional formula.

value.rationale: Second Veronese secants are the basic projective varieties of symmetric tensors of border rank at most two. Their equations and rank stratifications are classical, yet the theorem gives a complete topological phase law across every dimension and Veronese degree. The jump at d=2 has a structural explanation in the fixed monomials, and the exact-stratum formula shows that from d=3 onward compactly supported Euler characteristic is blind to Veronese degree. This is a natural global classification of a canonical invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
